newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker Maritime buys U.S. drill gear firm.
newsitem.headline: Aker Maritime buys U.S. drill gear firm.

text.p: Norwegian offshore services group Aker Maritime ASA said on Thursday it had acquired Texas-based company Pyramid, one of the world's largest suppliers of drilling derricks.
No sum was given for the deal.
Aker Maritime said the acquisition opened opportunities to increase sales of the Norwegian drilling concept, RamRig, in the Gulf of Mexico and other offshore markets in north and south America.

Developed by Aker Maritime subsidiary, Maritime Hydraulics, the first RamRig unit was ordered by U.S. drilling contractor Reading & Bates in March, 1996. Seven RamRig packages have been ordered to date amounting to 1.3 billion crowns.

Pyramid, with annual revenues of around $10 million, has a new manufacturing facility outside Houston and has a workforce of 70. It has delivered more than 2,000 drilling units, primarily for onshore oil and gas wells.
The group will be combined with Maritime Hydraulic's American operations.
